Evidence: PUT /api/studio/agents/:id/manifest: db.delete(agentSkills).where(agentId) then db.insert(agentSkills).values(skillIds) — direct table writes from a route, no withTransaction; invalidateAgentCaches only at :165 after both
Reproduction: PUT manifest with skillIds=[valid, unknown] → delete commits, insert throws FK 23503 → 500; agent left with ZERO skill links and caches stale up to 30s (invalidation never reached)
Root cause: REST handler owns a domain table and replaces links non-atomically; AGENTS.md §2 'REST handlers call gates, never services directly' + one-owner-per-table
Impact: Skill assignment data loss on partial failure; boundary rule broken; concurrent manifest writes can interleave delete/insert
Proposed fix: Add skillsGate.replaceAgentSkills(agentId, skillIds) doing withTransaction inside skill-service; route calls gate only
Required tests: Service test: replace with one bad id → all-or-nothing; route test: 404/400 mapping, links intact

Evidence: Executor resolves agent row from workspace DB (agentDb) but authorization calls skillsGate.getResolvedToolsForAgent(agentId) with no db threading — service uses ambient getDb() (ALS or global pool)
Reproduction: Split-DB workspace (x-workspace-id → tenant DB): writes via routes land in tenant DB; a run executed outside ALS (worker/socket) authorizes against global pool → skill grants invisible → tools denied, or wrong grants if same agentId exists there
Root cause: Ambient-only DB access in skill-service; no db/workspace param on any port (documented gap)
Impact: Multi-DB only: authorization may disagree with the agent row's DB (fail-closed denial or cross-DB grant); single-DB unaffected
Proposed fix: Thread workspace db: runWithDb around skills reads in executor, or add optional db/workspaceId to getResolvedToolsForAgent
Required tests: Integration: split-DB fixture asserts resolved tools match tenant rows
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07: tool-executor.ts:358-361 binds agentDb via runWithDb around skillsGate.getResolvedToolsForAgent; regression skill-service.test.ts:529 (split-DB two-tenant fixture); evidence npx vitest run src/skills = 39 passed, npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit = exit 0

Evidence: invalidateAgentCaches(agentId) deletes only the (dbScopeKey() + ':' + agentId) key of the CALLING scope; readers in another scope (global vs wsN, rotated handle) keep their entry. Comment claims 'scope-less clear only ever causes extra misses, never stale' — true only for the no-id clear
Reproduction: Workspace-scoped REST write invalidates wsN; a run/worker reading without ALS caches under 'global' → stale grant/tool list up to 30s TTL
Root cause: Scope-keyed invalidation assumes writer and reader share the same ALS handle; not guaranteed (workers, sockets, handle rotation)
Impact: Bounded (<=30s) stale authorization decisions after assignment/toolkit changes; extra misses acceptable but staleness is not documented as such
Proposed fix: Invalidate by agentId across scopes (TtlCache.invalidatePrefix(':agentId') suffix match) or add a per-agent generation counter checked on read
Required tests: Unit: two-scope cache — write in scope A, read scope B sees fresh after invalidate
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07: invalidateAgentCaches suffix-matches :agentId across scopes (skill-service.ts:79-81 + ttl-cache.ts:50-57 invalidateSuffix); regression skill-service.test.ts:551 (two-scope cache test, mutation-checked: fails on old scope-keyed delete); evidence npx vitest run src/skills = 39 passed, npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit = exit 0

Evidence: DB categorySchema = ['cognitive','operational','swarm','general'] (default general); Markdown SKILL_CATEGORIES = 3 values, 'general' is a parse error; doc claims closed §20 taxonomy
Reproduction: Create skill via REST with category default → 'general' accepted; same skill as Markdown rejected
Root cause: Two halves implement different taxonomies; doc describes only one
Impact: Skills created through REST cannot round-trip to Markdown; taxonomy claim in docs is half-true
Proposed fix: Align enums (drop 'general' or add a documented 4th) or document the DB/markdown split explicitly in Domain Spec
Required tests: Validator test pinning enum; parser test for 'general'

Evidence: listSummaries loads+parses every file body then discards bodies; getMarkdownSkill re-loads the whole directory per call; middleware does 1 list + 1 getSkill per triggered skill → k+1 full directory reads per turn
Reproduction: Workspace with 20 skill files: every context assembly reads/stats/parses all files 1..k+1 times; load_skill single-id path does the same
Root cause: No per-turn cache/memo; store is stateless per call
Impact: Latency + disk churn per turn scales with skill count; token economy unaffected
Proposed fix: Load directory once per turn (pass loaded set), or mtime/short-TTL cache in store; keep parse-failure semantics
Required tests: Store test: single load serves list+expand; middleware perf test with N files

Evidence: Docblock: 'A skill with NO trigger always lands in its full form'. Code: triggersFor() returns [] for names with no >=4-char word; branch requires triggers.length > 0 && matches → such a skill is always deferred, never expanded automatically
Reproduction: Install Markdown skill named 'QA' (no topic) → listed as deferred every turn, never auto-expanded; contradicts the stated baseline-specialization contract
Root cause: Comment written for an intended behavior the code does not implement
Impact: Agent never auto-applies short-named skills; doc/comment drift
Proposed fix: Either treat triggers.length===0 as alwaysOn (match comment) or fix the comment and Domain Spec
Required tests: Middleware test: triggerless skill → pinned expected block

Evidence: catch {} on DB skill load (no log) and catch {} on Markdown load (store logs internally but load-level failure silent)
Reproduction: DB outage → assigned skills silently vanish from prompt; no warn/telemetry
Impact: Failures invisible to operators; behavior differs silently from docs 'No PG / no roster: Markdown skills still apply'

Evidence: Universal list exists 3x: service 7 ids; executor fallback 5 (missing lock_in/lock_out); middleware 4. Executor also re-adds 5 hardcoded ids in isAllowed
Reproduction: Change/rename a universal in one place → authorization, schema injection, and fallback disagree
Impact: Renamed/added universals drift; executor fallback can authorize an id the resolver wouldn't (or vice versa)
Proposed fix: Export UNIVERSAL_TOOL_IDS from skills gate; all three import it
Required tests: Contract test: single exported list used by all three call sites

Evidence: update() = getById() then merge over existing then UPDATE; two concurrent partial updates both read pre-state; promptLayer merge uses stale existing → last-write-wins over the whole layer for overlapping keys
Reproduction: Concurrent PUT name-only + PUT executionGuidelines-only on same skill → one update's promptLayer merge can drop the other's change
Impact: Lost updates on concurrent edits (single-user low impact; agents/studio concurrent edits possible)
Proposed fix: SQL-level jsonb merge or optimistic updatedAt guard (WHERE updated_at = existing.updatedAt)
Required tests: Unit: interleaved updates keep both changes or 409

Reproduction: Direct gate caller passes NaN/10.5 → NaN/10.5 reaches drizzle limit

Evidence: composeSkills concatenates every resolved body (each capped 50k) with no total cap; load_skill returns it into the model context
Reproduction: load_skill with 10 x 50k skills → ~500k chars in one tool result/prompt block
Root cause: Per-file cap only, no aggregate cap
Impact: Prompt bloat / provider limit errors on multi-skill composition
Proposed fix: Total-size cap with explicit truncation report (e.g. 120k) + tests
Required tests: Store test: aggregate cap + truncated flag surfaced to load_skill

Evidence: enabled parses explicit falsy tokens; any other token (e.g. 'flase') → enabled=true silently
Reproduction: Typo enabled: flase → skill enabled although author intended off
Root cause: Closed-set discipline applied to category/workflow but not enabled
Impact: Silently enabled skill; mild surprise, no security impact
Proposed fix: Reject unknown enabled tokens or warn in report
Required tests: Parser test: unknown token → error or documented default
